title: Sync a local folder to a remote server with rsync, checking a dry run first
summary: rsync copies only the files that changed to a folder on another machine over SSH. A dry run first lists what would be copied without touching anything, so you can read the list before the real copy.

aliases.text: copy only changed files to remote
скопировать только изменённые файлы на сервер

steps.explain: Dry run: show what would be copied without changing anything. -n is the dry run. Lines starting with >f are files that would be sent, and cd lines are folders. The trailing slash on the local folder means copy its contents.
steps.expect: The list of files to send, then 'total size is ... (DRY RUN)'.

placeholders.name: LOCAL_DIR
placeholders.description: Local folder to send (its contents are copied)

placeholders.name: REMOTE_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder on the server that receives the copy

steps.explain: Read the list before you go on. Stop if a file is missing from it or if a line starts with *deleting. A deleting line means the server would lose a file, so the command has --delete in it; remove that option.
Real copy: send the changed files over SSH. Files that exist on the server with a different size or time are overwritten with your local copy.
steps.expect: Progress lines, then 'sent ... bytes  received ...' and 'total size is ... speedup is ...'.

placeholders.name: LOCAL_DIR
placeholders.description: Local folder to send (its contents are copied)

placeholders.name: REMOTE_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder on the server that receives the copy

steps.explain: Run the dry run again. An empty result (the text 'server matches the local folder') means nothing is left to send.
steps.cmd: rsync -avhn --itemize-changes -e ssh <LOCAL_DIR>/ <REMOTE_USER>@<REMOTE_HOST>:<REMOTE_DIR>/ | grep -E '^[<>]f' || echo "server matches the local folder"

placeholders.name: LOCAL_DIR
placeholders.description: Local folder to send (its contents are copied)

placeholders.name: REMOTE_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder on the server that receives the copy

rollback.explain: rsync cannot undo an overwrite. Restore the old version from a backup you made of the server folder before the copy, which is why you take one first.

warnings: Do not add --delete unless the dry run shows exactly the files you want removed on the server.
Files that are newer on the server are overwritten too. Add -u to skip files that are newer on the receiving side.
Without the trailing slash after the local folder, the folder itself is copied inside the target instead of its contents.
